newsitem.title: UK: UK govt testing water for budget betrayal - Lilley.
newsitem.headline: UK govt testing water for budget betrayal - Lilley.

text.p: Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer Peter Lilley on Monday accused the Labour government of "testing the water" ahead of Wednesday's budget for a betrayal of their election promises not to raise taxes.
In a statement, Lilley said Labour would not escape if it broke these pledges. "If they break their promises, we (the Conservatives) will never allow them to forget it," he said.
Lilley said that stories had been floated in newspapers in recent days suggesting a range of possible tax rises.
"Labour are testing the water for a betrayal of trust on Wednesday," he said.

"We will judge the Budget against Labour's pre-election commitments," he added, citing a statement by Tony Blair -- now Prime Minister -- that "We've no plans to increase tax at all." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
